Task: Streaming Speech-to-Text

Write code that handles partial and final streaming recognition events using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Transcribe Streaming:
  Service: Amazon Transcribe Streaming
  SDK: amazon-transcribe / boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_stream_transcription
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transcribe/latest/dg/streaming.html

Option 2 — DashScope Real-time ASR:
  Service: DashScope real-time speech recognition
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: RecognitionCallback, streaming call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/real-time-speech-recognition

Option 3 — Azure Speech Streaming:
  Service: Azure AI Speech streaming
  SDK: azure-cognitiveservices-speech
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: start_continuous_recognition, recognized
  Setup hints: AZURE_SPEECH_KEY, AZURE_SPEECH_REGION
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/speech-service/how-to-recognize-speech

Option 4 — Watson STT WebSocket:
  Service: Watson Speech to Text WebSocket
  SDK: ibm-watson
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: recognize_using_websocket
  Setup hints: IBM_STT_APIKEY, IBM_STT_URL
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/docs/speech-to-text?topic=speech-to-text-websockets

Option 5 — Deepgram:
  Service: Deepgram Streaming API
  SDK: deepgram-sdk
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: listen.websocket, transcribe
  Setup hints: DEEPGRAM_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://developers.deepgram.com/docs/lower-level-websockets

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

import asyncio
import os
import wave
from queue import Queue

import azure.cognitiveservices.speech as speechsdk

# This example simulates an audio stream from a WAV file.
# In a real application, you would typically get audio from a microphone or network stream.

def transcribe_streaming_audio(audio_filepath: str):
<GAP>
    speech_config = speechsdk.SpeechConfig(
        subscription=os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_KEY"),
        region=os.environ.get("AZURE_SPEECH_REGION")
    )
    speech_recognizer = speechsdk.SpeechRecognizer(
        speech_config=speech_config,
        audio_config=audio_config
    )

    all_results = []
    done = asyncio.Event()

    def recognized_cb(evt: speechsdk.SpeechRecognitionEventArgs):
        if evt.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.RecognizedSpeech:
            all_results.append(f"FINAL: {evt.result.text}")
        elif evt.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.NoMatch:
            all_results.append("NOMATCH: Speech could not be recognized.")
        elif evt.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.Canceled:
            cancellation_details = evt.result.cancellation_details
            all_results.append(f"CANCELED: Reason={cancellation_details.reason}")
            if cancellation_details.reason == speechsdk.CancellationReason.Error:
                all_results.append(f"CANCELED: ErrorCode={cancellation_details.error_code}")
                all_results.append(f"CANCELED: ErrorDetails={cancellation_details.error_details}")
            done.set()

    def recognizing_cb(evt: speechsdk.SpeechRecognitionEventArgs):
        if evt.result.reason == speechsdk.ResultReason.RecognizingSpeech:
            all_results.append(f"PARTIAL: {evt.result.text}")

    def session_stopped_cb(evt: speechsdk.SessionEventArgs):
        all_results.append(f"Session stopped event. {evt}")
        done.set()

    def canceled_cb(evt: speechsdk.SpeechRecognitionCanceledEventArgs):
        all_results.append(f"CANCELED: Reason={evt.reason}")
        if evt.reason == speechsdk.CancellationReason.Error:
            all_results.append(f"CANCELED: ErrorCode={evt.error_code}")
            all_results.append(f"CANCELED: ErrorDetails={evt.error_details}")
        done.set()

    speech_recognizer.recognized.connect(recognized_cb)
    speech_recognizer.recognizing.connect(recognizing_cb)
    speech_recognizer.session_stopped.connect(session_stopped_cb)
    speech_recognizer.canceled.connect(canceled_cb)

    # Start continuous recognition
    speech_recognizer.start_continuous_recognition()

    # Read audio from file and push to the push audio input stream
    with wave.open(audio_filepath, 'rb') as wf:
        if wf.getnchannels() != 1 or wf.getsampwidth() != 2 or wf.getframerate() != 16000:
            raise ValueError("Audio file must be mono, 16-bit PCM, 16kHz sample rate.")
        
        chunk_size = 1024  # bytes
        while True:
            audio_buffer = wf.readframes(chunk_size // wf.getsampwidth())
            if not audio_buffer:
                break
            push_stream.write(audio_buffer)
            # Simulate real-time audio by pausing
            # time.sleep(len(audio_buffer) / wf.getframerate() / wf.getsampwidth()) # This is a rough simulation
            
    push_stream.close() # Signal end of audio stream

    # Wait for recognition to complete
    asyncio.run(done.wait())
    speech_recognizer.stop_continuous_recognition()

    return all_results
